Based on my research, here are the common themes and connections among the five films **"I Love You, Man," "The Muppets," "Knocked Up," "This Is 40," and "Jeff, Who Lives at Home"**:

## Primary Connection: The Jason Segel Factor
The strongest unifying element is **Jason Segel's involvement** in multiple ways across these films:

**As Actor:**
- *I Love You, Man* (2009) - co-star alongside Paul Rudd
- *Knocked Up* (2007) - supporting role
- *This Is 40* (2012) - cameo/reprised role from *Knocked Up*
- *Jeff, Who Lives at Home* (2011) - lead role as Jeff

**As Creator:**
- *The Muppets* (2011) - co-writer and driving force behind reviving the franchise
- Also served as executive producer on the film

## Judd Apatow Collaboration Network
These films represent a close-knit creative community:

**Apatow Universe Overlap:**
- *Knocked Up* - written/directed by Judd Apatow
- *This Is 40* - Apatow spin-off/sequel to *Knocked Up*
- *I Love You, Man* - director John Hamburg previously worked with Segel on Apatow's *Undeclared*
- Many cast members (Segel, Rudd, Mann, Rogen) appear across multiple films

**Common Cast Members:**
- Paul Rudd appears in both *I Love You, Man* and *This Is 40*
- Jason Segel connects *Knocked Up* to its sequel *This Is 40*
- Leslie Mann appears in *Knocked Up* and stars in *This Is 40*

## Thematic Connections

**Coming-of-Age/Personal Growth Stories:**
- *I Love You, Man*: Man struggling to make male friends before marriage
- *Jeff, Who Lives at Home*: 30-year-old finding purpose through destiny
- *This Is 40*: Couples facing mid-life crises
- *Knocked Up*: Unexpected pregnancy forcing maturity

**Comedy-Drama Blending:**
- All films mix genuine emotional moments with comedy
- Focus on relatable, imperfect characters
- Balance between humor and heartfelt storytelling

## Creative Philosophy

**Ensemble-Driven Storytelling:**
- Multiple relationship dynamics rather than single protagonist focus
- Rich supporting casts with interconnected storylines
- Improvisational elements, particularly in Apatow-produced work

**Authentic Character Development:**
- Characters feel like real people with recognizable flaws
- Focus on contemporary relationship challenges
- Grounded comedy stemming from everyday situations

These films essentially represent a particular era of American comedy (roughly 2007-2012) characterized by:
- The Apatow comedy style
- Jason Segel's leading man emergence
- Blending of mainstream appeal with indie sensibilities
- Focus on extended adolescence and delayed adulthood themes

Their connection comes less from shared storylines and more from the creative ecosystem and collaborative approach that defined this generation of comedy filmmakers.

***Forgetting Sarah Marshall*** is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Nicholas Stoller (in his feature directorial debut) and starring Jason Segel, Kristen Bell, Mila Kunis and Russell Brand. The film, which was written by Segel and co-produced by Judd Apatow, was released by Universal Pictures. Filming began in April 2007 at the Turtle Bay Resort on the North Shore of Oahu Island in Hawaii. The film was released for North American theaters on April 18, 2008, and in the United Kingdom a week later on April 25, 2008.


The story revolves around Peter Bretter, who is a music composer for a TV show that features his girlfriend, Sarah Marshall, in the lead role. After a five-year relationship, Sarah abruptly breaks up with Peter. Devastated by this event, he chooses to go on vacation to Hawaii, in order to try to move forward with his life. Trouble ensues when he runs into Sarah on the island as she is on vacation with her latest boyfriend.

***Jeff, Who Lives at Home*** is a 2011 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Jay and Mark Duplass, starring Jason Segel and Ed Helms, and co-starring Judy Greer and Susan Sarandon.[3] The film premiered on September 14, 2011, at the 2011 Toronto International Film Festival and then saw a limited release in the United States and Canada on March 16, 2012,[4] after having been pushed back from the original date of March 2.[5] The film received praise for its humor, but grossed only $4.7 million worldwide against a $7.5 million budget.[6]




## Plot

[edit]

Jeff is a 30-year-old unemployed stoner living in his mother Sharon's basement in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. He looks for his destiny in seemingly random occurrences. Finding inspiration in the film *Signs* reinforces his belief in this.

**Jason Jordan Segel** (/ˈsiːɡəl/ *SEE-gəl*; born January 18, 1980) is an American actor. He is best known for his role as Marshall Eriksen in the CBS sitcom *How I Met Your Mother* from 2005 to 2014. He began his career with director and producer Judd Apatow on the television series *Freaks and Geeks* (1999–2000) and *Undeclared* (2001–2002) before gaining prominence for his leading roles in various successful comedy films in which he has starred, written, and produced.

Segel had recurring roles on *CSI: Crime Scene Investigation* as Neil Jansen and on *Undeclared* as Eric. He played Marshall Eriksen on the CBS sitcom *How I Met Your Mother*; he had previously stated he would move on to other projects in 2013 when his contract expired,[21] but was convinced to finish the series after its ninth season in 2014.[22]


Segel made his film debut with *Can't Hardly Wait* in 1998. His other early feature film appearances include *Slackers*, *SLC Punk!*, *The Good Humor Man*, and *Dead Man on Campus*. In 2007, he appeared in *Knocked Up*, directed by *Freaks and Geeks* producer Judd Apatow. Segel starred in the lead role of 2008's *Forgetting Sarah Marshall*, a film he wrote and Apatow produced with Shauna Robertson for Universal Pictures. He also starred in *I Love You, Man*, which was released on March 20, 2009, by DreamWorks.[23]

***Sex Tape*** is a 2014 American sex comedy film directed by Jake Kasdan and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. It was written by Jason Segel, Nicholas Stoller, and Kate Angelo and stars Segel, Cameron Diaz, Rob Corddry, Ellie Kemper, and Rob Lowe. Its story follows a married couple who make a sex tape to spice up their relationship only to wake up the next morning to find that it has gone missing. This sparks a frantic search in an attempt to find it.


The film was produced by Columbia Pictures and was released on July 18, 2014. It grossed $14.6 million in its opening weekend and $126.1 million worldwide, against a budget of $40 million.[3] It received generally negative reviews.[4]

Jay and Annie Hargrove are a married couple who used to have sex at every opportunity. Now, after having two kids, they rarely are intimate.

***Our Friend*** is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Gabriela Cowperthwaite and written by Brad Ingelsby, based on Matthew Teague's 2015 *Esquire* article "The Friend: Love Is Not a Big Enough Word". It stars Jason Segel, Dakota Johnson, and Casey Affleck.


The film had its world premiere under its original title ***The Friend*** at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival on September 6, 2019, and was released on January 22, 2021, by Gravitas Ventures. It was a box-office bomb, only grossing $714,255 on a $10 million budget.[2][3]




## Plot

[edit]

In the winter of 2013, Matt and Nicole Teague prepare to tell their daughters, Molly and Evie, that Nicole's ovarian cancer is terminal. Outside, their best friend Dane Faucheux keeps the children company.


</fragment>
<fragment>
Review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes reported that 85% of 113 critics gave the film a positive review, with an average rating of 7.3/10. The site's critics consensus reads: "*Our Friend*'s occasionally frustrating approach to dramatizing its fact-based story is often offset by a trio of starring performances led by a never-better Jason Segel."[13] Metacritic assigned the film a weighted average score of 57 out of 100, based on 20 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[14]


Ella Kemp from *The Playlist* praised the performances stating: "The Friend is successfully anchored by its three leading players... The sensitivity of these performances, particularly from Affleck and Segel, offers a reckoning on sincere friendship and the limits of devotion that remains with the viewer, long after the days of waiting and the years of pain have finally come to an end."[15]

<title>Jason Segel</title>
<fragment>

Segel had recurring roles on *CSI: Crime Scene Investigation* as Neil Jansen and on *Undeclared* as Eric. He played Marshall Eriksen on the CBS sitcom *How I Met Your Mother*; he had previously stated he would move on to other projects in 2013 when his contract expired,[21] but was convinced to finish the series after its ninth season in 2014.[22]


Segel made his film debut with *Can't Hardly Wait* in 1998. His other early feature film appearances include *Slackers*, *SLC Punk!*, *The Good Humor Man*, and *Dead Man on Campus*. In 2007, he appeared in *Knocked Up*, directed by *Freaks and Geeks* producer Judd Apatow. Segel starred in the lead role of 2008's *Forgetting Sarah Marshall*, a film he wrote and Apatow produced with Shauna Robertson for Universal Pictures. He also starred in *I Love You, Man*, which was released on March 20, 2009, by DreamWorks.[23]

The film opened on October 30, 2015, alongside *Burnt* and *Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse*. In its opening weekend, it was projected to make $5–7 million from 2,202 theaters,[23] however only ended up grossing $3.2 million, finishing eighth at the box office. This was the lowest wide release opening of Bullock's career, beating 1996's *Two If by Sea* ($4.7 million).[24] In it second weekend the film made $1.4 million, finishing 11th.[25]



### Critical response

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

***Our Brand Is Crisis*** is a 2015 American comedy-drama film directed by David Gordon Green and written by Peter Straughan, based on the 2005 documentary film of the same name by Rachel Boynton. The film gives a fictionalized account of the involvement of American political campaign strategists Greenberg Carville Shrum (GCS) in the 2002 Bolivian presidential election. The film stars Sandra Bullock, Scoot McNairy, Billy Bob Thornton, Anthony Mackie, Ann Dowd and Joaquim de Almeida.


Principal photography began on September 29, 2014, in New Orleans, Louisiana. George Clooney and Grant Heslov produced. The film was screened in the Special Presentations section of the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival.[4] It was theatrically released by Warner Bros. on October 30, 2015. It received mixed reviews, despite Bullock's performance being largely praised, and was a box office disappointment.

Segel had recurring roles on *CSI: Crime Scene Investigation* as Neil Jansen and on *Undeclared* as Eric. He played Marshall Eriksen on the CBS sitcom *How I Met Your Mother*; he had previously stated he would move on to other projects in 2013 when his contract expired,[21] but was convinced to finish the series after its ninth season in 2014.[22]


Segel made his film debut with *Can't Hardly Wait* in 1998. His other early feature film appearances include *Slackers*, *SLC Punk!*, *The Good Humor Man*, and *Dead Man on Campus*. In 2007, he appeared in *Knocked Up*, directed by *Freaks and Geeks* producer Judd Apatow. Segel starred in the lead role of 2008's *Forgetting Sarah Marshall*, a film he wrote and Apatow produced with Shauna Robertson for Universal Pictures. He also starred in *I Love You, Man*, which was released on March 20, 2009, by DreamWorks.[23]

**Jason Jordan Segel** (/ˈsiːɡəl/ *SEE-gəl*; born January 18, 1980) is an American actor. He began his career with director and producer Judd Apatow on the television series *Freaks and Geeks* (1999–2000) and *Undeclared* (2001–2002) before gaining prominence for his leading roles in various successful comedy films in which he has starred, written, and produced.

The website's critical consensus reads, "While certainly overlong, *The Five-Year Engagement* benefits from the easy chemistry of its leads and a funny, romantic script with surprising depth and intelligence."[7] On Metacritic the film has a score of 62 out of 100 based on 38 reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews."[8] Audiences surveyed by CinemaScore gave the film a grade B− on scale of A to F.[1][9]


Owen Gleiberman Entertainment Weekly gave the film a grade of a B+ and called it "A lively, original, and scattershot-hilarious ramble of a Judd Apatow production."[10] Elizabeth Weitzman, from *New York Daily News* wrote: "Blunt has never been more relaxed, and she and Segel have a believably warm chemistry."[11] Richard Roeper gave the film a grade of a B+, saying that it featured a "winning cast in an uneven but often brilliant and weird comedy."[12]

***Can't Hardly Wait*** is a 1998 American teen romantic comedy film written and directed by Deborah Kaplan and Harry Elfont. It stars an ensemble cast including Ethan Embry, Charlie Korsmo, Lauren Ambrose, Peter Facinelli, Seth Green, and Jennifer Love Hewitt, and is notable for a number of "before-they-were-famous" appearances by teen stars. The story takes place at a high school graduation party in the 1990s.


The film received mixed reviews from critics. It grossed a total of $25 million at the North American domestic box office, against a production budget of $10 million. The soundtrack peaked at number 25 on the *Billboard* 200 chart.

## Sequel

[edit]

On May 25, 2019, on Danny Pellegrino's *Everything Iconic* podcast, Jennifer Love Hewitt revealed that she is developing *Can't Hardly Wait 2* with plans to direct it herself. The concept revolves around the reunion of the original high school gang from the 1998 film.[17]



## Home media

[edit]

The film was released on VHS and DVD on November 17, 1998.[18] On September 30, 2008, it was re-released on DVD and Blu-ray as the "10 Year Reunion Edition" to commemorate the film's 10th anniversary. The re-release included bonus features not on the original release.[19] Mill Creek Entertainment reissued the DVD and Blu-ray on June 17, 2014 and October 30, 2018 respectively with the latter format billed as the "20 Year Reunion Edition".

<fragment>

***Our Friend*** is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Gabriela Cowperthwaite and written by Brad Ingelsby, based on Matthew Teague's 2015 *Esquire* article "The Friend: Love Is Not a Big Enough Word". It stars Jason Segel, Dakota Johnson, and Casey Affleck.


The film had its world premiere under its original title ***The Friend*** at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival on September 6, 2019, and was released on January 22, 2021, by Gravitas Ventures. It was a box-office bomb, only grossing $714,255 on a $10 million budget.[2][3]




## Plot

[edit]

In the winter of 2013, Matt and Nicole Teague prepare to tell their daughters, Molly and Evie, that Nicole's ovarian cancer is terminal. Outside, their best friend Dane Faucheux keeps the children company.


</fragment>
<fragment>
Review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes reported that 85% of 113 critics gave the film a positive review, with an average rating of 7.3/10. The site's critics consensus reads: "*Our Friend*'s occasionally frustrating approach to dramatizing its fact-based story is often offset by a trio of starring performances led by a never-better Jason Segel."[13] Metacritic assigned the film a weighted average score of 57 out of 100, based on 20 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[14]

***Jeff, Who Lives at Home*** is a 2011 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Jay and Mark Duplass, starring Jason Segel and Ed Helms, and co-starring Judy Greer and Susan Sarandon.[3] The film premiered on September 14, 2011, at the 2011 Toronto International Film Festival and then saw a limited release in the United States and Canada on March 16, 2012,[4] after having been pushed back from the original date of March 2.[5] The film received praise for its humor, but grossed only $4.7 million worldwide against a $7.5 million budget.[6]




## Plot

[edit]

Jeff is a 30-year-old unemployed stoner living in his mother Sharon's basement in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. He looks for his destiny in seemingly random occurrences. Finding inspiration in the film *Signs* reinforces his belief in this.

***Our Friend*** is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Gabriela Cowperthwaite and written by Brad Ingelsby, based on Matthew Teague's 2015 *Esquire* article "The Friend: Love Is Not a Big Enough Word". It stars Jason Segel, Dakota Johnson, and Casey Affleck.


The film had its world premiere under its original title ***The Friend*** at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival on September 6, 2019, and was released on January 22, 2021, by Gravitas Ventures. It was a box-office bomb, only grossing $714,255 on a $10 million budget.[2][3]




## Plot

[edit]

In the winter of 2013, Matt and Nicole Teague prepare to tell their daughters, Molly and Evie, that Nicole's ovarian cancer is terminal. Outside, their best friend Dane Faucheux keeps the children company.

Ella Kemp from *The Playlist* praised the performances stating: "The Friend is successfully anchored by its three leading players... The sensitivity of these performances, particularly from Affleck and Segel, offers a reckoning on sincere friendship and the limits of devotion that remains with the viewer, long after the days of waiting and the years of pain have finally come to an end."[15]

Based on my searches of Wikipedia articles, here's an overview of the indie drama films starring Jason Segel:

## **The End of the Tour** (2015)
- **Director:** James Ponsoldt
- **Co-stars:** Jesse Eisenberg
- **Key Details:** Segel portrays author David Foster Wallace, with Eisenberg playing Rolling Stone journalist David Lipsky. The film is based on Lipsky's book "Although of Course You End Up Becoming Yourself," which chronicles his interviews with Wallace at the end of his book tour for "Infinite Jest." 
- **Awards Recognition:** Segel received critical acclaim and multiple award nominations for his performance, including nominations from Chicago Film Critics Association, Independent Spirit Awards, and Chlotrudis Society for Independent Films.

## **The Discovery** (2017)
- **Director:** Charlie McDowell
- **Co-stars:** Rooney Mara, Jesse Plemons, Riley Keough, Robert Redford
- **Key Details:** A science fiction romance film. Segel stars alongside Rooney Mara in this Netflix original that premiered at Sundance in January 2017. The film explores themes of life after death through a scientist's discovery of proof of the afterlife.
- **Production:** Filmed in Newport, Rhode Island in March 2016.

## **Come Sunday** (2018)
- **Director:** Joshua Marston
- **Co-stars:** Chiwetel Ejiofor, Condola Rashad, Lakeith Stanfield, Danny Glover, Martin Sheen
- **Key Details:** Based on a "This American Life" episode, this Netflix film tells the story of evangelist Carlton Pearson (Ejiofor) who had a crisis of faith. Segel plays a supporting role in this drama about faith and doubt. Premiered at Sundance in January 2018.

## **Our Friend** (2019)
- **Director:** Gabriela Cowperthwaite
- **Co-stars:** Dakota Johnson, Casey Affleck
- **Key Details:** A biographical drama based on Matthew Teague's Esquire article "The Friend: Love Is Not a Big Enough Word." Segel plays Dane Faucheux, the best friend who helps care for his friend's family when the wife is diagnosed with terminal cancer. The film premiered at Toronto International Film Festival in 2019 and received strong reviews, particularly for Segel's performance, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 85% positive reviews.

**Common Elements:**
- All four films premiered at major film festivals (Sundance or Toronto)
- All are dramatic departures from Segel's earlier comedy work
- Three of the four were distributed by Netflix
- All showcase Segel's serious dramatic acting abilities
- The films received generally positive critical reception, with particular praise for Segel's performances

These films represent Jason Segel's successful transition from comedy to more dramatic, indie film work, demonstrating his range as an actor and his ability to tackle complex, emotionally demanding roles.

## Sequel

[edit]

On May 25, 2019, on Danny Pellegrino's *Everything Iconic* podcast, Jennifer Love Hewitt revealed that she is developing *Can't Hardly Wait 2* with plans to direct it herself. The concept revolves around the reunion of the original high school gang from the 1998 film.[17]



## Home media

[edit]

The film was released on VHS and DVD on November 17, 1998.[18] On September 30, 2008, it was re-released on DVD and Blu-ray as the "10 Year Reunion Edition" to commemorate the film's 10th anniversary. The re-release included bonus features not on the original release.[19] Mill Creek Entertainment reissued the DVD and Blu-ray on June 17, 2014 and October 30, 2018 respectively with the latter format billed as the "20 Year Reunion Edition".

Other positive reviews come from *Entertainment Weekly* who gave the film a B+ and applauded "Jason Segel's riff on varieties of male bewilderment,"[18] and Mick LaSalle of the *San Francisco Chronicle*, who wrote "Segel's breakthrough movie, *Forgetting Sarah Marshall*, deserves to ride the wave of the latest, hottest micro-trend in pictures: the romantic comedy for guys."[19]



## Awards and nominations

[edit]

*Forgetting Sarah Marshall* was nominated for five awards at the 2008 Teen Choice Awards, but did not win any of them. The nominations were:[20]



* Movie, Bromantic Comedy
* Movie, Actress Comedy: Kristen Bell
* Movie, Breakout Female: Kristen Bell
* Movie, Breakout Female: Mila Kunis
* Movie, Breakout Male: Jason Segel


On *The Comedy Festival Presents: Funniest Movies of the Year 2008* on TBS, *Forgetting Sarah Marshall* was voted "The Funniest Film of 2008".

![](image)Mann in 2008
Mann began her career at 18, appearing in a number of television commercials. In 1996, she appeared in *The Cable Guy*, followed with performances in *Freaks & Geeks*, Sam Weisman's *George of The Jungle* alongside Brendan Fraser, *Big Daddy* with Adam Sandler, *Orange County* opposite Jack Black, and *The 40-Year-Old Virgin* with Steve Carell.[9]


In 2007, Mann starred alongside Seth Rogen and Paul Rudd in Judd Apatow's comedy *Knocked Up*, which grossed more than $218 million worldwide.[10] Her performance brought rave reviews and a "Best Supporting Actress" nomination from the Chicago Film Critics Association. The film won the People's Choice Award for "Favorite Movie Comedy", was named one of AFI's "Top Ten Films of the Year", and received a "Best Comedy" nomination from the Broadcast Film Critics Association Awards.[11]

***A Family Affair*** is an upcoming American romantic comedy film directed by Richard LaGravenese and written by Carrie Solomon. The film stars Nicole Kidman, Zac Efron, Joey King, Liza Koshy, and Kathy Bates.


*A Family Affair* is set to be released by Netflix on an unspecified date in 2024.




## Premise

[edit]

A young woman named Zara works as an assistant for movie star Chris Cole that is until Chris falls in love with her mother.



## Cast

[edit]

* Zac Efron as Chris Cole
* Joey King as Zara
* Nicole Kidman
* Liza Koshy
* Kathy Bates


## Production

[edit]

Filming took place in Atlanta from August to October 2022.[2][3]



## Release

[edit]

*A Family Affair* was scheduled to be released by Netflix on November 17, 2023.[4] However, the release of the film was postponed with a new release date yet to be set, due to the impact of the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike in the United States on the film's promotion.[5]

## Sequel

[edit]

On May 25, 2019, on Danny Pellegrino's *Everything Iconic* podcast, Jennifer Love Hewitt revealed that she is developing *Can't Hardly Wait 2* with plans to direct it herself. The concept revolves around the reunion of the original high school gang from the 1998 film.[17]



## Home media

[edit]

The film was released on VHS and DVD on November 17, 1998.[18] On September 30, 2008, it was re-released on DVD and Blu-ray as the "10 Year Reunion Edition" to commemorate the film's 10th anniversary. The re-release included bonus features not on the original release.[19] Mill Creek Entertainment reissued the DVD and Blu-ray on June 17, 2014 and October 30, 2018 respectively with the latter format billed as the "20 Year Reunion Edition".

***Can't Hardly Wait*** is a 1998 American teen romantic comedy film written and directed by Deborah Kaplan and Harry Elfont. It stars an ensemble cast including Ethan Embry, Charlie Korsmo, Lauren Ambrose, Peter Facinelli, Seth Green, and Jennifer Love Hewitt, and is notable for a number of "before-they-were-famous" appearances by teen stars. The story takes place at a high school graduation party in the 1990s.


The film received mixed reviews from critics. It grossed a total of $25 million at the North American domestic box office, against a production budget of $10 million. The soundtrack peaked at number 25 on the *Billboard* 200 chart.

<fragment>

***I Love You, Man*** is a 2009 American bromantic comedy film written and directed by John Hamburg, based on a script by Larry Levin. The film stars Paul Rudd as a friendless man looking for a best man for his upcoming wedding. However, his new best friend (Jason Segel) is straining his relationship with his bride (Rashida Jones).


The film was released theatrically in the United States on March 20, 2009, to mostly positive reviews.[3] The film grossed $92 million on a $40 million budget. It marked the third collaboration between Segel and Rudd, after *Knocked Up* (2007) and *Forgetting Sarah Marshall* (2008).




## Plot

[edit]

Peter Klaven, a Los Angeles real estate agent, proposes to his girlfriend Zooey Rice, and she accepts. He does not have any close male friends to share the news with, only family and mainly female acquaintances. After overhearing her friends' concern over his lack of guy friends, Peter decides he needs to find some to have a best man for the wedding.


</fragment>
<fragment>
![](image)Sign at Paramount Theatre in Austin, Texas advertising the premiere of the film
On Rotten Tomatoes the film has an approval rating of 83% based on 207 reviews, with an average rating of 6.9/10. The website's critical consensus states, "*I Love You, Man* makes the most of its simple premise due to the heartfelt and hilarious performances of Paul Rudd and Jason Segel."[21] On Metacritic the film has a weighted average score of 70 out of 100, based on 34 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[22] Audiences surveyed by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of "B+" on scale of A+ to F.[23]

- The film was noted for showcasing the chemistry between Segel and Rudd

Other positive reviews come from *Entertainment Weekly* who gave the film a B+ and applauded "Jason Segel's riff on varieties of male bewilderment,"[18] and Mick LaSalle of the *San Francisco Chronicle*, who wrote "Segel's breakthrough movie, *Forgetting Sarah Marshall*, deserves to ride the wave of the latest, hottest micro-trend in pictures: the romantic comedy for guys."[19]



## Awards and nominations

[edit]

*Forgetting Sarah Marshall* was nominated for five awards at the 2008 Teen Choice Awards, but did not win any of them. The nominations were:[20]



* Movie, Bromantic Comedy
* Movie, Actress Comedy: Kristen Bell
* Movie, Breakout Female: Kristen Bell
* Movie, Breakout Female: Mila Kunis
* Movie, Breakout Male: Jason Segel


On *The Comedy Festival Presents: Funniest Movies of the Year 2008* on TBS, *Forgetting Sarah Marshall* was voted "The Funniest Film of 2008".



## Follow-up spin-off

[edit]

Main article: Get Him to the Greek


</fragment>
<fragment>

***Forgetting Sarah Marshall*** is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Nicholas Stoller (in his feature directorial debut) and starring Jason Segel, Kristen Bell, Mila Kunis and Russell Brand. The film, which was written by Segel and co-produced by Judd Apatow, was released by Universal Pictures. Filming began in April 2007 at the Turtle Bay Resort on the North Shore of Oahu Island in Hawaii. The film was released for North American theaters on April 18, 2008, and in the United Kingdom a week later on April 25, 2008.


The story revolves around Peter Bretter, who is a music composer for a TV show that features his girlfriend, Sarah Marshall, in the lead role. After a five-year relationship, Sarah abruptly breaks up with Peter. Devastated by this event, he chooses to go on vacation to Hawaii, in order to try to move forward with his life. Trouble ensues when he runs into Sarah on the island as she is on vacation with her latest boyfriend.

***Jeff, Who Lives at Home*** is a 2011 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Jay and Mark Duplass, starring Jason Segel and Ed Helms, and co-starring Judy Greer and Susan Sarandon.[3] The film premiered on September 14, 2011, at the 2011 Toronto International Film Festival and then saw a limited release in the United States and Canada on March 16, 2012,[4] after having been pushed back from the original date of March 2.[5] The film received praise for its humor, but grossed only $4.7 million worldwide against a $7.5 million budget.[6]

***Sex Tape*** is a 2014 American sex comedy film directed by Jake Kasdan and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. It was written by Jason Segel, Nicholas Stoller, and Kate Angelo and stars Segel, Cameron Diaz, Rob Corddry, Ellie Kemper, and Rob Lowe. Its story follows a married couple who make a sex tape to spice up their relationship only to wake up the next morning to find that it has gone missing. This sparks a frantic search in an attempt to find it.


The film was produced by Columbia Pictures and was released on July 18, 2014. It grossed $14.6 million in its opening weekend and $126.1 million worldwide, against a budget of $40 million.[3] It received generally negative reviews.[4]

<title>Slackers (film)</title>
<fragment>

***Slackers*** is a 2002 American comedy film directed by Dewey Nicks and starring Jason Schwartzman, Devon Sawa, Jason Segel, Michael Maronna, Jaime King, and Laura Prepon. Its plot follows a nerdy college student who blackmails a group of young men with his knowledge that they have cheated throughout college, and uses it to get closer to a young woman he is obsessed with. This was Mamie Van Doren's second to last movie (*The American Tetralogy* 2012), she starred naked at the age of 71.[3]




## Plot

[edit]

* Gina Gershon as Woman at Trendy Club (uncredited)

## Soundtrack

[edit]

The film has a few tracks from Handsome Boy Modeling School (Prince Paul & Dan The Automator), including "Holy Calamity" and "Rock & Roll (Could Never Hip-Hop Like This)". It has a symphonic instrumental performance of "Baba O'Riley" from The Who playing over the opening credits, as well as an A Capella performance of "The Sign" by Ace of Base (sung by a college choir) during a scene.

<document>
<title>Jason Segel</title>
<fragment>

Segel had recurring roles on *CSI: Crime Scene Investigation* as Neil Jansen and on *Undeclared* as Eric. He played Marshall Eriksen on the CBS sitcom *How I Met Your Mother*; he had previously stated he would move on to other projects in 2013 when his contract expired,[21] but was convinced to finish the series after its ninth season in 2014.[22]


Segel made his film debut with *Can't Hardly Wait* in 1998. His other early feature film appearances include *Slackers*, *SLC Punk!*, *The Good Humor Man*, and *Dead Man on Campus*. In 2007, he appeared in *Knocked Up*, directed by *Freaks and Geeks* producer Judd Apatow. Segel starred in the lead role of 2008's *Forgetting Sarah Marshall*, a film he wrote and Apatow produced with Shauna Robertson for Universal Pictures. He also starred in *I Love You, Man*, which was released on March 20, 2009, by DreamWorks.[23]


</fragment>
<fragment>

Following elementary school and middle school, Segel completed his high school studies at Harvard-Westlake School, where his 6 ft 4 in (1.93 m) frame helped him as an active member of the 1996 and 1997 CIF state champion boys' basketball team.[16][17] He won a slam dunk contest in high school[18] and he was nicknamed "Dr. Dunk."[19] He was a backup to the team's star center, Jason Collins, who went on to play in the NBA.[16]



## Career

[edit]

![A man holds a microphone as he speaks](image)Segel at the Austin premiere of *I Love You, Man* in 2009
Segel's first major role was as stoner "freak" Nick Andopolis on the critically acclaimed but short-lived 1999 NBC comedy-drama series *Freaks and Geeks*. The series revolved around a group of suburban Detroit high school students circa 1980. Segel personally composed a song for his character, Nick, to sing to the lead female character, Lindsay (Linda Cardellini).[20]

<title>Can't Hardly Wait</title>
<fragment>

***Can't Hardly Wait*** is a 1998 American teen romantic comedy film written and directed by Deborah Kaplan and Harry Elfont. It stars an ensemble cast including Ethan Embry, Charlie Korsmo, Lauren Ambrose, Peter Facinelli, Seth Green, and Jennifer Love Hewitt, and is notable for a number of "before-they-were-famous" appearances by teen stars. The story takes place at a high school graduation party in the 1990s.


The film received mixed reviews from critics. It grossed a total of $25 million at the North American domestic box office, against a production budget of $10 million. The soundtrack peaked at number 25 on the *Billboard* 200 chart.

The script for *Can't Hardly Wait* was originally written in 1996, by Harry Elfont and Deborah Kaplan who were looking for a project they could develop and direct themselves on a limited budget. The project was approved by Columbia Pictures in mid-1997, following the success of teen-oriented horror film *Scream* in early 1997.[6] Principal photography for *Can't Hardly Wait* started in October 1997, and ran for 26 days.[6] Jennifer Love Hewitt was known for *Party of Five* when she signed on to the film, and appeared in the slasher hit *I Know What You Did Last Summer*, which helped to further raise her profile.[6] According to Charlie Korsmo, Adam Hann-Byrd was originally cast as William Lichter.[7]


The cast had a week of rehearsals before filming.[1]


The film initially received an R-Rating due to MPAA objections about the depiction of teens drinking alcohol at an unsupervised party and drug use. The film was recut to receive a PG-13 rating.[1]

***Dead Man on Campus*** is a 1998 black comedy film starring Tom Everett Scott and Mark-Paul Gosselaar. It centers on the urban legend that a student gets straight As if their roommate commits suicide (*see* pass by catastrophe). ## Plot

[edit]

Josh gets into college on a scholarship, and Cooper is assigned as his roommate. Cooper does little work and instead spends all the time partying and consistently fails his courses, but his father continues to pay his tuition. ## Jason Segel's Films (1998-2006)

### 1998 - Film Debut
**Can't Hardly Wait** - Segel made his film debut as "Matt, Watermelon Guy" in this teen romantic comedy ensemble film featuring many "before-they-were-famous" young actors.

**Dead Man on Campus** - He played "Kyle" in this black comedy about college students trying to trigger an academic loophole by finding a suicidal roommate. The film also featured future collaborators Alyson Hannigan and Linda Cardellini.

**SLC Punk!** - Segel appeared in this cult punk rock film starring Matthew Lillard, playing an unnamed supporting role.

### 2002
**Slackers** - Segel played Sam Schecter, one of the lead roles alongside Devon Sawa and Jason Schwartzman in this college comedy about cheating students being blackmailed.

### Career Pattern 1998-2006
- **Supporting roles**: During this period, Segel primarily appeared in supporting or ensemble roles rather than leading
- **Teen/college comedies**: Most of his early film work was in youth-oriented comedies
- **Collaboration network**: He worked with actors who would become frequent collaborators, including Linda Cardellini and Alyson Hannigan
- **Television focus**: His primary career breakthrough during 1998-2006 came from television, particularly "Freaks and Geeks" (1999-2000) and "Undeclared" (2001-2002)

### Notable Gap
It appears Segel's film career was relatively sparse between 2002-2006, likely focusing more on television work until his major film breakthrough with "Forgetting Sarah Marshall" (2008), which he also wrote.

### Key Career Development
This period (1998-2006) represents Segel's early career establishment phase, where he built his acting foundation in ensemble comedies before transitioning to leading roles and screenwriting in later years. ***The Five-Year Engagement*** is a 2012 romantic comedy film written, directed, and produced by Nicholas Stoller. Produced with Judd Apatow and Rodney Rothman, it is co-written by Jason Segel, who also stars in the film with Emily Blunt as a couple whose relationship becomes strained when their engagement is continually extended. The film was released in North America on April 27, 2012[3] and in the United Kingdom on June 22, 2012.[4]




## Plot

[edit]

In San Francisco, sous-chef Tom, and PhD graduate Violet, are happily engaged. Their wedding plans are interrupted when Tom's best friend Alex gets Violet's sister Suzie pregnant at Tom and Violet's engagement party, and Alex and Suzie quickly marry. When Violet is accepted into the University of Michigan's two-year post-doctorate psychology program, Tom agrees to move with her and delay their wedding, but is disheartened to learn his boss planned to make him a head chef.

Based on my research of various Jason Segel films, here are the interesting plot elements and key aspects you should know about several of his notable movies:

## **Forgetting Sarah Marshall (2008)**
- **Written by and starring Jason Segel**, this was his breakthrough leading role
- **Plot**: Peter Bretter (Segel) is a music composer for a TV show starring his girlfriend Sarah Marshall (Kristen Bell). After she abruptly breaks up with him after 5 years, he goes to Hawaii to recover, only to find Sarah vacationing there with her new boyfriend Aldous (Russell Brand)
- **Notable element**: Features a **full-frontal nude breakup scene** that was quite controversial and often discussed
- **Muppet connection**: The film includes a puppet musical Segel's character is working on, foreshadowing his later Muppets work

## **I Love You, Man (2009)**
- **Third collaboration** between Segel and Paul Rudd (after Knocked Up and Forgetting Sarah Marshall)
- **Plot**: Paul Rudd plays a friendless man who needs a best man for his wedding. He forms an unlikely friendship with Segel's character, which strains his relationship with his fiancée (Rashida Jones)
- **Bromantic comedy** - essentially a romantic comedy about male friendship
- **Casting chemistry**: It only took one lunch to get Segel and Rudd to sign on, which helped attract other actors

## **The Five-Year Engagement (2012)**
- **Co-written by Segel** with director Nicholas Stoller
- **Plot**: A couple (Segel and Emily Blunt) keep delaying their wedding due to career opportunities and life circumstances
- **Filmed in Ann Arbor** with some authentic local references
- **Critical reception**: Generally favorable reviews, praised for the chemistry between leads and intelligent script despite being overlong

## **The End of the Tour (2015)**
- **Critically acclaimed dramatic performance** by Segel as author David Foster Wallace
- **Plot**: Based on a book by David Lipsky about his five-day interview with Wallace following the publication of "Infinite Jest"
- **Critical consensus**: 92% on Rotten Tomatoes, with Segel's performance called "brilliantly performed" and "stunning"
- **A dramatic departure** from his typical comedy roles, showing serious acting range

## **The Discovery (2017)**
- **Science fiction romance** available on Netflix
- **Plot**: In a world where the existence of the afterlife has been scientifically proven, Segel plays a man who visits the island where the discovery was made and falls for a mysterious woman
- **Star-studded cast**: Co-stars Rooney Mara, Jesse Plemons, Riley Keough, and Robert Redford
- **Unique premise**: Explores philosophical questions about life, death, and purpose in a sci-fi context

## **General Patterns:**
- Segel often **co-writes his films** (Forgetting Sarah Marshall, The Five-Year Engagement)
- Many of his films involve **relationship struggles** and **personal growth**
- He has great **chemistry with co-stars** like Paul Rudd, Kristen Bell, and Emily Blunt
- Shows range from **broad comedies** to **intimate dramas** like The End of the Tour

These films showcase Segel's evolution from comedy supporting roles to leading man status, demonstrating both his comedic timing and dramatic capabilities.

**Allison Lee Hannigan** (born March 24, 1974), known professionally as **Alyson Hannigan**, is an American actress and television presenter.[1] After starting her career at age four with appearances in commercials, she moved to Hollywood at age 11 and soon got an agent.

**Allison Lee Hannigan** (born March 24, 1974), known professionally as **Alyson Hannigan**, is an American actress and television presenter.[1] After starting her career at age four with appearances in commercials, she moved to Hollywood at age 11 and soon got an agent.


</fragment>
<fragment>

Hannigan began her film career with supporting roles in the comedy films *Impure Thoughts* (1986) and *My Stepmother Is an Alien* (1988), getting a Young Artist Award nomination for the latter. In 1999, she began starring in the *American Pie* film series as Michelle Flaherty, the films' primary love interest, appearing in every film in the series from 1999 to 2012. For her role in the series, she was nominated for three Teen Choice Awards and won a Young Hollywood Award. She went on to star in the parody film *Date Movie* (2006), the slasher film *You Might Be the Killer* (2018), and the superhero film *Flora & Ulysses* (2021).

Anna Friel was originally attached as the female lead, but Friel pulled out shortly before filming started due to reported "creative differences" and was replaced by Claire Forlani.[6] Reports differed over whether Friel was fired or quit due to unhappiness with the script.[2]


The film features a dance number similar to *She's All That* wherein everyone dances to the song "Stop the Rock" by Apollo 440. Forlani said she was given minimal notice to do it, saying "They literally pull me into this room with 30 dancers who for two days have been learning a routine that I have to learn in half an hour. And it was really complicated, too. I was in the corner … and they ordered like, the Gap kids … and I thought, 'Oh f\*\*\*, I'm doomed! And Freddie said, 'Oh, I can do it.' And I said, 'Well, that's because you're not meant to get it right.'"[7]
